newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T won't comment on Reynolds price move.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T won't comment on Reynolds price move.

text.p: Tobacco to insurance company B.A.T Industries Plc declined to comment on the impact of a decision by RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co to raise wholesale cigarette prices by $0.04 per pack.
"This is an issue for Brown & Williamson and B.A.T declines to comment," said Ralph Edmondson, a spokesman for B.A.T
The Reynolds price increase, effective Friday, puts $2 per 1,000 cigarettes on all products except its Century brand.
Analysts said RJ Reynolds raised prices about a month sooner than expected.
"Usually what happens is the two big ones (Reynolds and Philip Morris Cos Inc ) move and then the two smaller ones follow," said one analyst.
"They will be looking at how the price increases have been taken across the brands and how the trade has taken to them before they move," he added.

Brown & Williamson, a subsidiary of B.A.T, has about 17 percent of the U.S. cigarette market, compared with Reynolds 26 percent and Philip Morris 46 percent. B&W's American brands include Kool and GPC.
